messages:
rachel: Quick announcement  we're rolling out an automated API-diff report and a short release freeze for API surface changes. Goal: make docs + SDK releases safer and reduce surprise breakages. Please read the rollout note: https://redwood.internal/docs/api-diff-rollout
tom: Nice. How does the API-diff work? Is it schema driven or AST diff?
rachel: It runs a combination of signature/AST diffs for typed SDKs and runtime shape checks for untyped. CI will post a markdown report to the PR showing added/removed/changed fields and a "severity" tag (info / minor / major).
priya: New process asks: any PR with severity >= minor must attach a migration checklist + a snippet for at least one language. Correct?
rachel: Correct. The PR template will now include a "migration-checklist" section and a generated migration-snippet artifact (JS + Python) if the diff detects renamed params or changed defaults.
release-bot: Scheduled job: api-diff-scan at 2025-03-03T14:00Z. CI check name: redwood/api-diff.
docs-bot: Docs impact: we'll auto-generate a "What changed" page and a machine-readable migration manifest that feeds the release notes. Docs team will also add a severity legend and examples.
tom: Will the severity tagging be editable by reviewers? Sometimes the classifier mislabels a behavior change.
rachel: Yes, reviewers can override and must add rationale in the PR body. The CLA will require an explicit "severity-confirmed" checkbox before merge.
oliver: Release cadence question: does this change the release window? We're already doing weekly patches.
priya: For API-surface changes were introducing a 14-day freeze window before a public minor/major release. That means any severity >= minor must land and sit in canary for at least 14 days with the migration manifest published. Non-API patches can continue on the weekly cadence.
tom: Can we scope the freeze to only SDK packages that touched public types?
priya: Yes, the automation will detect affected packages and only apply the freeze to those. Other packages can be released as usual.
docs-bot: Example CLI usage to generate the report locally:```
# from repo root
yarn redwood-api-diff --from=v1.12.0 --to=HEAD --out=./api-diffs/v1.12.0-head.md
```
rachel: We'll also surface anonymized telemetry about which migration snippets are downloaded so we know which code paths customers adapt. Telemetry is opt-out at org-level.
oliver: Enterprise exception process? Some customers will need more runway.
priya: Open a support ticket with label "api-freeze-exempt". PM + Eng + CSM review within 72h; if approved, we can pin a compatibility flag per-tenant or publish a tailored migration plan.
tom: QA: add e2e tests that run the generated migration snippet against a small sample app so we can catch obvious regressions. I'll add that to the pipeline.
rachel: Docs team will create a lightweight template for the migration checklist and ship a docs-linter rule that blocks merges without it. ETA: docs template + CI rule by EOD Friday.
priya: I'll update the release playbook and post a short FAQ for Eng + Support.
release-bot: Release checklist created: https://redwood.internal/board/api-diff-launch  status: in review.
rachel: Thanks all 4dd. If you need early access to the canary or want to opt-out of telemetry for a project, DM me or open a ticket.
